A stronger model may help, but it does not fundamentally solve the prompt specialization problem. The trade-
off can still persist when multiple review objectives compete within one prompt.

C. Provide the full repository as context instead of just the changed files and surrounding code, giving the
model deeper visibility into business logic. (Incorrect)

More context increases cost and complexity and may even dilute attention. The observed issue stems from
balancing multiple review goals, not a lack of repository-wide context.

D. Replace the few-shot examples with a detailed checklist of specific logic edge cases to verify, such as
division-by-zero in score calculation or grading thresholds. (Incorrect)

Checklists can help for known cases but are less effective than dedicated, specialized review passes. They
also do not address the underlying competition between business-logic and API-design review objectives
within a single prompt.

questions.question: Production monitoring shows the research phase takes longer than expected. Analysis reveals the coordinator invokes the web search subagent, then invokes the document analysis subagent and waits again. These tasks are independent--neither requires the other's output. What is the most effective way to run these subagents concurrently?

options.A: Switch both subagents to use a Haiku-tier model instead of Sonnet to reduce their individual execution time.
options.B: Create an async orchestration layer outside the agent that spawns parallel threads, each running a separate coordinator.
options.C: Structure the coordinator to emit both Task tool calls (for web search and document analysis) in a single response message.
options.D: Add detailed instructions to the coordinator's system prompt explaining the performance benefits of parallel execution at the same time.

questions.explanation:
C. Structure the coordinator to emit both Task tool calls (for web search and document analysis) in a single
response message. (Correct)

This enables true concurrent execution at the tool-calling layer. Since the web search and document
analysis subagents are independent, issuing both tool calls in the same coordinator response allows the
runtime to execute them in parallel instead of waiting for one to finish before starting the other. This directly
removes the sequential bottleneck without changing model quality or adding unnecessary system complexity.

A. Switch both subagents to use a Haiku-tier model instead of Sonnet to reduce their individual execution
time. (Incorrect)

This reduces per-task latency but does not address the core inefficiency, which is sequential execution, not
model speed.

B. Create an async orchestration layer outside the agent that spawns parallel threads, each running a
separate coordinator. (Incorrect)

This introduces unnecessary architectural complexity and duplicates coordination logic when parallelism can
already be achieved within a single coordinator response.

D. Add detailed instructions to the coordinator's system prompt explaining the performance benefits of
parallel execution at the same time. (Incorrect)

Prompt instructions alone cannot guarantee parallel execution; only structured multi-tool invocation can
enforce concurrency.

questions.question: Your development team is using Claude Code to automate test generation across a large codebase. However, developers are frequently rejecting the generated test suites because Claude creates a high volume of trivial assertions or tests that merely maximize line coverage without validating meaningful behavioral logic or edge cases. You want to guide Claude to generate high-quality, production-ready tests directly without introducing high latency or modifying the core pipeline script. Which strategy best ensures that high-quality, meaningful tests are generated in the first place?

options.A: Restrict test generation to directories where historical quality metrics show higher acceptance rates, disabling it for areas where generated tests consistently require heavy editing.
options.B: Add post-generation coverage analysis that automatically filters out any generated test that doesn't increase line coverage beyond what existing tests provide.
options.C: Document testing standards in CLAUDE.md including valuable test criteria, available fixtures with intended use cases, and examples distinguishing meaningful behavioral tests from trivial assertions.
options.D: Implement a two-phase generation where a second Claude call scores each test against quality criteria, filtering out low-scoring tests before presenting results to developers.

questions.explanation:
C. Document testing standards in CLAUDE.md including valuable test criteria, available fixtures with
intended use cases, and examples distinguishing meaningful behavioral tests from trivial assertions. 
Correct

Why C is correct:

CLAUDE.md provides persistent guidance that shapes test generation from the start. By documenting quality
standards, fixtures, and examples of meaningful behavioral tests, Claude is more likely to generate
production-ready tests that validate logic and edge cases instead of chasing line coverage.

A. Restrict test generation to certain directories Incorrect
Limits where tests are generated but does not improve test quality.

B. Add post-generation coverage analysis Incorrect
Coverage increases do not guarantee meaningful or high-quality tests.

D. Implement a second scoring call Incorrect
Can filter poor tests but adds latency and modifies the pipeline, which the requirements explicitly avoid.

questions.question: A developer uses Claude Code to refactor a function during their development session. Before committing, they ask the same Claude session to review the code for issues. Later, a separate automated CI review catches several bugs that the same-session review missed. What best explains this discrepancy?

options.A: The CI environment has access to the full codebase context while the local session only sees the current file
options.B: The CI review uses a more specific prompt tailored for catching bugs, while the developer's request was too general
options.C: Claude retains context about its prior reasoning in the session, making it less likely to question its own decisions
options.D: The extended session length caused the context window to fill with conversation history, leaving less room for thorough analysis

questions.explanation:
C. Claude retains context about its prior reasoning in the session, making it less likely to question its own
decisions. Correct

Why C is correct:

When Claude reviews code in the same session where it created or refactored the code, it retains its earlier
reasoning and assumptions. This can lead to confirmation bias, making it less likely to critically re-evaluate its
own changes. A fresh CI review starts with no prior attachment to those decisions and may identify issues that
the same-session review misses.

A. The CI environment has access to the full codebase context while the local session only sees the current
file Incorrect

Local sessions can also access the codebase using file-reading and navigation tools; this is not the primary
reason for the discrepancy.

B. The CI review uses a more specific prompt tailored for catching bugs, while the developer's request was
too general Incorrect

Prompt quality can affect results, but the key issue described is reviewing code within the same session that
generated it.

D. The extended session length caused the context window to fill with conversation history, leaving less
room for thorough analysis Incorrect

Long conversations may affect context management, but this is not the main explanation for missing bugs
that a fresh review catches.

questions.question: Your codebase exploration tool stores session IDs to allow engineers to continue investigations across work sessions. An engineer spent an hour yesterday analyzing a legacy authentication module, building context about its architecture and dependencies. They want to continue today. The session ID is valid, but version control shows 3 of the 12 files the agent previously read were modified overnight by a teammate's merge. What approach best balances efficiency and accuracy?

options.A: Resume the session and immediately have the agent re-read all 12 previously analyzed files to ensure complete alignment.
options.B: Resume the session without informing the agent about the changed files, allowing it to naturally detect discrepancies during execution.
options.C: Resume the session and inform the agent which specific files changed for targeted re-analysis while retaining context on the unchanged files.
options.D: Start a fresh session to ensure the agent works with current codebase state without stale assumptions from the previous day.

questions.explanation:
C. Resume the session and inform the agent which specific files changed for targeted re-analysis while
retaining context on the unchanged files. Correct

Why C is correct:

This approach preserves the valuable context built during the previous session while ensuring accuracy by re-
analyzing only the files that changed. It balances efficiency and correctness by avoiding unnecessary re-
reading of unchanged files and preventing stale assumptions.

A. Resume the session and immediately have the agent re-read all 12 previously analyzed files to ensure

complete alignment. Incorrect
Ensures freshness but is inefficient because nine files remain unchanged.

B. Resume the session without informing the agent about the changed files, allowing it to naturally detect
discrepancies during execution. Incorrect
Risks relying on outdated assumptions and missing the impact of recent changes.

D. Start a fresh session to ensure the agent works with current codebase state without stale assumptions
from the previous day. Incorrect
Guarantees fresh context but discards an hour of useful analysis and is unnecessarily inefficient.

questions.question: An engineer sees an unfamiliar error message "SYNC_CONFLICT: entity version mismatch detected" in production logs but doesn't know which of the 12 services in the codebase generates it. They ask the agent to help locate the source code. What exploration approach will most efficiently find the responsible code?

options.A: Use Grep to search for distinctive text from the error message (like "SYNC_CONFLICT" or "entity version mismatch"), then Read the matching files to understand context.
options.B: Use Glob to find files in directories commonly associated with error handling (such as errors/, exceptions/, or handlers/) across services, then Read each matching file.
options.C: Use Grep to find all files that import the project's error handling module, then Read those files to locate custom error definitions.
options.D: Read the project's README and service configuration files to understand the architecture, then systematically Read source files in service directory.

questions.explanation:
A. Use Grep to search for distinctive text from the error message (like "SYNC_CONFLICT" or "entity
version mismatch"), then Read the matching files to understand context. Correct
Why A is correct:

Searching for unique strings in the error message is the fastest and most direct way to locate the source code
that generates the error. Grep quickly identifies matching files, and Read provides the surrounding context to
determine which service is responsible.

B. Use Glob to find files in error-related directories Incorrect
Error messages may not be defined in dedicated error directories, making this approach inefficient and
incomplete.

C. Use Grep to find all files that import the project's error handling module Incorrect
Many files may import the error module, creating numerous irrelevant matches and increasing investigation
time.

D. Read the project's README and service configuration files Incorrect
Provides architectural context but is a slow, indirect approach for locating a specific error message.

questions.question: After expanding the agent's MCP tools with delivery-specific capabilities [apply_promo_code, update_delivery_address, reconcile_delivery], the total tool count has grown from 1 to 7. We have observed that the agent now shows tool selection accuracy has dropped from 86% to 71%. Log analysis reveals the majority of errors involve the agent selecting between semantically overlapping tools -- calling issue_credit when process_refund was correct, and calling check_delivery_status when looking order_allready_returns_the_needed_data. Which approach structurally eliminate the semantic overlap identified in the error source?

options.A: Consolidate semantically overlapping tools � merge issue_credit and process_refund into a single handle_promotions tool with an action parameter and fold check_delivery_status into lookup_order with an optional include_tracking flag.
options.B: Enable the tool search tool with defer_loading on the six new tools, keeping the original two always loaded, so the agent dynamically discovers specialized tools only when needed.
options.C: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt demonstrating correct selection for each ambiguous tool, such as showing when issue_credit applies versus when process_refund is appropriate.
options.D: Split the tools across two sub-agents -- a 'financial resolution' agent with issue_credit, process_refund, return_order, and apply_promo_code and a 'delivery operations' agent with the remaining delivery tools -- with a coordinating routing between them.

questions.explanation:
A. Consolidate semantically overlapping tools � merge issue_credit and process_refund into a single
handle_promotions tool with an action parameter and fold check_delivery_status into lookup_order with an
optional include_tracking flag. Correct

Why A is correct:

The primary issue is semantic overlap between tools. When multiple tools perform similar functions or return
overlapping information, the agent struggles to choose correctly. Consolidating overlapping tools into unified
interfaces removes ambiguity and structurally improves tool selection accuracy.

B. Enable tool search with defer_loading Incorrect

Reduces the number of simultaneously loaded tools but does not eliminate the underlying semantic overlap.

C. Add few-shot examples Incorrect

Examples may improve selection temporarily, but they do not address the root cause of overlapping tool
capabilities.

D. Split tools across two sub-agents Incorrect

Domain separation can help organization, but overlap still exists within domains (for example, issue_credit vs.
process_refund), so ambiguity remains.

questions.question: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. An engineer submits two requests: Request A: "Rename the getUserData function to fetchUserProfile everywhere it's used." Request B: "Improve error handling throughout the data processing module--add try/catch blocks, meaningful error messages, and ensure failures don't silently corrupt data." For which request does specifying an explicit multi-phase workflow (such as analyze propose implement with review) most improve outcome quality?

options.A: Neither request benefits significantly
options.B: Request A, the function rename task
options.C: Both requests benefit equally
options.D: Request B, the error handling task

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Neither request benefits significantly
Request B is a complex, judgment-heavy change that benefits substantially from a structured workflow.
B. Incorrect Request A, the function rename task
A global function rename is usually a relatively mechanical refactor. Tools like Grep, language-aware rename
features, and tests often make this straightforward.
C. Incorrect Both requests benefit equally
While both can benefit from planning, the improvement in quality is much greater for Request B.
D. Correct Request B, the error handling task
Improving error handling requires understanding control flow, identifying failure points, preserving data
integrity, avoiding unintended side effects, and designing consistent error messages and recovery behavior. A

multi-phase workflow such as analyze propose implement review helps the agent reason about the
module before making broad changes, leading to higher-quality and safer results.

Final Answer: D

questions.question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Your pipeline includes a release-notes generation step that classifies and summarizes approximately 200 commits at the end of each weekly release cycle. Each commit is currently sent as a separate Messages API request using a Sonnet-tier Claude model. The release notes are not needed until the following morning, providing approximately 12 hours of acceptable latency. Your team must reduce the per-token API cost while retaining the same model, prompts, and output quality. Which approach satisfies all these constraints?

options.A: Issue the 200 Messages API requests concurrently because parallel execution reduces the per-token price.
options.B: Submit the 200 requests through the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values and retrieve the results after the batch finishes.
options.C: Concatenate all 200 commit messages into one Messages API request because reducing the number of requests always reduces token costs.
options.D: Replace the Sonnet-tier model with a Haiku-tier model to obtain a lower per-token price.

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Issue the 200 Messages API requests concurrently because parallel execution reduces the
per-token price.

Concurrency may reduce total wall-clock time, but it does not reduce the per-token API cost.

B. Correct Submit the 200 requests through the Message Batches API with unique custom_id values
and retrieve the results after the batch finishes.

The Message Batches API is designed for large numbers of independent requests where latency is not critical.
It allows you to keep the same model, prompts, and output quality while reducing cost for high-volume
asynchronous workloads such as release-note generation.

C. Incorrect Concatenate all 200 commit messages into one Messages API request because reducing
the number of requests always reduces token costs.

Combining all commits into one request changes the task structure, can affect output quality, may increase
context complexity, and does not guarantee lower token usage.

D. Incorrect Replace the Sonnet-tier model with a Haiku-tier model to obtain a lower per-token price.

This violates the requirement to retain the same model and preserve output quality.

Final Answer: B

questions.question: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems. Testing reveals that when source documents are missing certain specifications, the model fabricates plausible- sounding values to satisfy your schema's required fields. For example, a document mentioning only dimensions receives a fabricated "weight: 2.3 kg" in the extraction output. What schema design change most effectively addresses this hallucination behavior?

options.A: Add explicit instructions to the prompt stating "only extract information explicitly stated in the document; use placeholder text for missing values."
options.B: Change fields that may not exist in source documents from required to optional, allowing the model to omit them.
options.C: Add a "confidence" field alongside each specification where the model self-reports its certainty, then filter out low-confidence extractions.
options.D: Implement semantic validation that verifies each extracted value appears in or can be inferred from the source document text.

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Add explicit instructions to the prompt stating "only extract information explicitly stated in
the document; use placeholder text for missing values."

Prompt instructions help, but they do not remove the structural pressure created by a schema that requires
values for fields that may not exist.

B. Correct Change fields that may not exist in source documents from required to optional, allowing the
model to omit them.

The hallucination occurs because the schema requires a value for every field. Making potentially absent fields
optional removes the incentive to fabricate plausible values and allows the extraction to accurately represent
missing information.

C. Incorrect Add a "confidence" field alongside each specification where the model self-reports its
certainty, then filter out low-confidence extractions.

Confidence scores are not a reliable mechanism for preventing hallucinations, and fabricated values may still
be reported with high confidence.

D. Incorrect Implement semantic validation that verifies each extracted value appears in or can be
inferred from the source document text.

This is a useful downstream safeguard, but it is not the most effective schema design change to prevent the
behavior at its source.

Final Answer: B

questions.question: You are building developer-productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools--Read, Write, Bash, Grep, and Glob--and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Your productivity agent connects to three MCP servers: an issue tracker with search_issues , get_issue , and create_comment ; a documentation wiki with search_docs , get_page , and list_spaces ; and a database explorer with run_query , get_schema , and list_databases . For cross-system questions such as, "Which database tables are affected by the authentication refactor in PROJ-1234?", the agent makes eight to ten sequential exploratory calls, lacks visibility into each server's available content, and exhausts context before completing complex investigations. What architectural change best leverages MCP capabilities to address these problems?

options.A: Add a prepare_investigation tool to each server that accepts a natural-language question and returns relevant summaries.
options.B: Consolidate all three systems into one unified MCP server with cross-referencing capabilities.
options.C: Expose each server's content catalog as MCP resources, including issue summaries, documentation hierarchies, and database schemas.
options.D: Add an orchestrator that routes each question to one server based on keywords.

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Add a prepare_investigation tool to each server that accepts a natural-language question
and returns relevant summaries.

This may reduce some calls, but it does not solve the core problem of discoverability and context-efficient
exploration across systems.

B. Incorrect Consolidate all three systems into one unified MCP server with cross-referencing
capabilities.

This is a heavy operational change and is not necessary to take advantage of MCP's native strengths.

C. Correct Expose each server's content catalog as MCP resources, including issue summaries,
documentation hierarchies, and database schemas.

MCP resources are designed for discoverable, structured context. Exposing issue summaries, wiki structure,
and database schemas allows the agent to understand what content exists before making targeted tool calls,
reducing exploratory requests and preserving context for complex investigations.

D. Incorrect Add an orchestrator that routes each question to one server based on keywords.

Cross-system questions inherently require information from multiple servers, so single-server routing would
miss important relationships.

Final Answer: C

questions.question: The coordinator provides detailed step-by-step instructions to the web-search subagent, specifying exact search queries, source priorities, and date filters. Production monitoring reveals three issues: (1) the subagent reports "insufficient results" instead of trying alternative approaches when the specified searches fail, (2) research quality drops for emerging topics that do not match expected patterns, and (3) the subagent rarely surfaces valuable tangential sources. What is the most effective way to improve subagent adaptability?

options.A: Specify research objectives and quality criteria--such as coverage breadth, source diversity, and recency-- rather than prescribing procedural steps, allowing the subagent to determine its search strategy.
options.B: Remove procedural details entirely and delegate using simple goals such as "research this topic thoroughly," relying on the subagent's general capabilities.
options.C: Add fallback directives requiring alternative query formulations whenever the specified searches produce fewer than a predetermined number of results.
options.D: Classify each topic as either "well-defined" or "exploratory" and use a different instruction style for each category.

questions.explanation:
A. Correct Specify research objectives and quality criteria--such as coverage breadth, source diversity,
and recency--rather than prescribing procedural steps, allowing the subagent to determine its search
strategy.

This directly addresses all three problems:

The subagent can adapt when initial searches fail.
It can explore emerging topics that do not fit predefined query patterns.
It is encouraged to surface valuable tangential sources through broader, goal-oriented exploration.

B. Incorrect Remove procedural details entirely and delegate using simple goals such as "research this
topic thoroughly," relying on the subagent's general capabilities.

This gives too little guidance and may reduce consistency and quality control.

C. Incorrect Add fallback directives requiring alternative query formulations whenever the specified
searches produce fewer than a predetermined number of results.

This improves robustness for failed searches but does not solve the broader adaptability and source-
discovery issues.

D. Incorrect Classify each topic as either "well-defined" or "exploratory" and use a different instruction
style for each category.

This can help in some cases, but it is less effective than shifting from procedural control to objective-based
delegation across all research tasks.

Final Answer: A

questions.question: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. During initial testing of the automated review pipeline, you notice that reviews on large pull requests containing more than 50 changed files sometimes take over 20 minutes and cost $8�$12 per run because of extensive agentic loops. Claude reads files, runs analysis tools, and iterates many times. Your team needs each invocation to abort once it reaches both a fixed iteration count and a fixed dollar amount, enforced by Claude Code itself rather than by the surrounding job runner. Which configuration change directly enforces both per-invocation caps?

options.A: Switch the --model flag to a smaller, less expensive model so each iteration uses fewer tokens and has a lower per-call cost.
options.B: Set timeout-minutes: 5 on the GitHub Actions job step and monitor per-run costs through the Anthropic Console usage dashboard.
options.C: Add --max-turns 10 --max-budget-usd 2.00 to the claude -p invocation to cap iterations and spending.
options.D: Set --permission-mode dontAsk to automatically deny tool-permission requests not included in the explicitly allowed set.

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Switch the --model flag to a smaller, less expensive model so each iteration uses fewer
tokens and has a lower per-call cost.

This may reduce the average cost per run, but it does not enforce hard limits on either the number of
iterations or the total amount spent.

B. Incorrect Set timeout-minutes: 5 on the GitHub Actions job step and monitor per-run costs through
the Anthropic Console usage dashboard.

A GitHub Actions timeout stops the workflow externally. The question specifically requires the limits to be
enforced by Claude Code itself.

C. Correct Add --max-turns 10 --max-budget-usd 2.00 to the claude -p invocation to cap iterations and
spending.

These flags directly enforce a maximum number of agentic turns and a maximum dollar budget for that
specific invocation, which satisfies both requirements.

D. Incorrect Set --permission-mode dontAsk to automatically deny tool-permission requests not
included in the explicitly allowed set.

This controls tool-permission behavior, not the number of iterations or the spending limit.

Final Answer: C

questions.question: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks using built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Your agent has spent significant context exploring the rendering subsystem--reading shader code, buffer management, and frame synchronization logic. An engineer now asks it to understand how the physics engine integrates with rendering for collision debug overlays. You notice recent responses reference "typical rendering patterns" rather than the specific VulkanPipeline and FrameGraph classes it discovered earlier. What's the most effective approach to handle this transition while preserving accuracy?

options.A: Spawn a sub-agent to explore physics independently, then manually synthesize its findings with the rendering knowledge accumulated in the main conversation.
options.B: Use /clear to reset context completely, then start fresh with physics exploration using file paths from the project's CLAUDE.md.
options.C: Continue in the current context with more targeted prompts referencing the specific classes by name.
options.D: Summarize key rendering findings (including specific class names and architectural patterns), clear or reset the main context window (or delegate to a sub-agent seeded with that summary), then proceed with the physics integration exploration.

questions.explanation:
A. Incorrect Spawn a sub-agent to explore physics independently, then manually synthesize its findings
with the rendering knowledge accumulated in the main conversation.

This helps divide the work, but it does not solve the underlying problem that the main context is already
becoming degraded and losing project-specific accuracy.

B. Incorrect Use /clear to reset context completely, then start fresh with physics exploration using file
paths from the project's CLAUDE.md.

Resetting without preserving the important rendering discoveries risks losing the specific knowledge about
VulkanPipeline, FrameGraph, and the architectural relationships already uncovered.

C. Incorrect Continue in the current context with more targeted prompts referencing the specific
classes by name.

The observed behavior indicates that the context is already overloaded. Simply adding more targeted prompts
is unlikely to reliably restore the lost precision.

D. Correct Summarize key rendering findings (including specific class names and architectural
patterns), clear or reset the main context window (or delegate to a sub-agent seeded with that summary),
then proceed with the physics integration exploration.

This is the most effective approach because it preserves the high-value, project-specific rendering knowledge
while freeing context capacity for the new investigation. A concise architectural summary acts as a durable

bridge between the rendering and physics explorations and helps maintain accuracy during the transition.
Final Answer: D

questions.question: Your schema includes a 'skills: string[] field. Production monitoring reveals three consistency issues: (1) compound phrases like "Python and SQL" are sometimes kept as one entry, sometimes split; (2) implied but unstated skills occasionally appear in extractions; (3) similar documents produce wildly different array lengths (5-10 vs 40+ entries). Your prompt currently says "Extract all skills mentioned." What's the most effective improvement?

options.A: Add few-shot examples demonstrating compound phrase handling, explicit mention criteria, and appropriate entry granularity.
options.B: Add constraints: "Extract 10-20 skills maximum, one skill per entry, only explicitly named skills."
options.C: Add post-extraction normalization that maps skills to a canonical taxonomy and deduplicates similar entries.
options.D: Enrich the schema to skill: string, confidence: float, source_quote: string to capture extraction confidence.

questions.explanation:
A. Correct Add few-shot examples demonstrating compound phrase handling, explicit mention criteria,
and appropriate entry granularity.

Few-shot examples are the most effective improvement because they teach the model the desired extraction
behavior directly. They show how to split compound phrases consistently, include only explicitly mentioned
skills, and maintain a consistent level of granularity across documents. This addresses all three observed
inconsistencies without imposing arbitrary limits.

B. Incorrect Add constraints: "Extract 10-20 skills maximum, one skill per entry, only explicitly named
skills."

These constraints reduce variability, but a fixed maximum can truncate legitimate documents that contain
many skills and may reduce extraction completeness.

C. Incorrect Add post-extraction normalization that maps skills to a canonical taxonomy and
deduplicates similar entries.

Normalization helps downstream consistency, but it does not teach the model how to decide what counts as a
skill during extraction.

D. Incorrect Enrich the schema to skill: string, confidence: float, source quote: string to capture
extraction provenance.

This improves traceability and auditing, but it does not directly resolve the inconsistent extraction behavior.

Final Answer: A
